title: The weighted Bhatia–Kittaneh conjecture for positive semidefinite matrices
statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be $n\times n$ positive definite semidefinite matrices. For $t\in[0,1]$, let $\lambda_j$ denote the eigenvalues and $\sigma_j$ the singular values, indexed by $j=1,\ldots,n$. **Weighted Bhatia–Kittaneh conjecture.** For every $j=1,\ldots,n$, one has

$$
\lambda_j((1-t)A+tB)\geq\sqrt{\sigma_j(A^{2(1-t)}B^{2t})}.
$$

This conjecture proposes a singular-value strengthening of the weighted eigenvalue inequality discussed in the paper, extending the Bhatia–Kittaneh question beyond the established weighted result. Its resolution is not specified in the source.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.05525

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2016).
source_name: Minghua Lin, “On Drury's solution of Bhatia \& Kittaneh's question”, arXiv:1601.05525 (2016).
